[TritonNvidiaGPU] Prefer Two CTA layouts for two-CTA MMA (#10817)

With WS disabled, M-first CTA layouts improve 4/8-CTA matmul throughput
by 2–9% versus `main` (`f8cddb947b`) on GB200 (FP16, M=N=8192, SM cap
1.2 GHz; TFLOPS main → PR, reconstructed fixed configurations, 2×60
rotating rounds×32 launches).

| K | 2 CTAs, no WS | 4 CTAs, no WS | 8 CTAs, no WS |
| --: | --: | --: | --: |
| 64 | 169.8 → 170.0 | 148.7 → 153.7 | 144.7 → 148.2 |
| 512 | 810.8 → 807.8 | 468.0 → 493.5 | 529.5 → 542.3 |
| 2048 | 1189.5 → 1189.6 | 525.8 → 562.7 | 716.1 → 774.4 |
| 8192 | 1354.3 → 1335.9 | 531.4 → 579.3 | 743.9 → 805.6 |

[AMD] Re-enable kernarg preload under MIR dump/swap (#12654)

Kernarg preload has been disabled whenever TRITON_DUMP_MIR or
TRITON_SWAP_MIR is set, because the allocated preload SGPRs were not
serialized to MIR YAML: a dump/swap round trip silently lost the preload
and emitted a kernel that s_loads its arguments from memory. That meant
MIR captured for scheduling work did not describe the code Triton
actually ships.

LLVM now serializes that state
(https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/168374), so the guard can be
removed.

@@ -966,3 +966,104 @@ def test_mir_swap_enable_misched_requires_swap_mir(tmp_path):
     result = subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(script_file)], capture_output=True, text=True, env=env, timeout=120)
     assert result.returncode != 0
     assert "TRITON_SWAP_MIR_ENABLE_MISCHED requires TRITON_SWAP_MIR" in result.stderr
+
+
+def _run_kernel_script(script_file, env_overrides):
+    """Run a kernel script in a subprocess with a deterministic compilation env."""
+    import os
+    import subprocess
+    import sys
+
+    env = os.environ.copy()
+    env["TRITON_ALWAYS_COMPILE"] = "1"
+    # Line info perturbs the IR hash, and with it the name the dump is filed under.
+    env["TRITON_DISABLE_LINE_INFO"] = "1"
+    env.update(env_overrides)
+
+    result = subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(script_file)], capture_output=True, text=True, env=env, timeout=240)
+    assert result.returncode == 0, f"kernel script should succeed. stderr: {result.stderr[:2000]}"
+    return result
+
+
+def _amdgcn_from_stdout(text):
+    marker = "// -----// AMDGCN Dump //----- //"
+    assert marker in text, "AMDGCN_ENABLE_DUMP should have printed the AMDGCN"
+    return text.split(marker, 1)[1].strip()
+
+
+def _kernarg_preload_length(asm):
+    import re
+
+    match = re.search(r"^\s*\.amdhsa_user_sgpr_kernarg_preload_length\s+(\d+)", asm, re.MULTILINE)
+    return int(match.group(1)) if match else 0
+
+
+def _descriptor_directives(asm):
+    """The .amdhsa_* directives of the kernel descriptor, which encode the preload request."""
+    return [line.strip() for line in asm.splitlines() if line.strip().startswith(".amdhsa_")]
+
+
+def _normalized_instructions(asm):
+    """Instruction lines with register numbers erased, so allocator tie-breaking does not count."""
+    import re
+
+    out = []
+    for line in asm.splitlines():
+        line = line.split(";", 1)[0].split("//", 1)[0].strip()
+        if not line or line.startswith(".") or line.endswith(":"):
+            continue
+        line = re.sub(r"[sv]\[[0-9:]+\]", "R", line)
+        line = re.sub(r"\b[sv][0-9]+\b", "R", line)
+        out.append(line)
+    return out
+
+
+def test_kernarg_preload_state_is_serialized_to_mir(tmp_path):
+    """Preloaded kernarg SGPRs must appear in the dumped MIR, not be silently dropped."""
+    script_file = tmp_path / "test_kernel.py"
+    script_file.write_text(_SIMPLE_KERNEL_SCRIPT)
+
+    clean = _run_kernel_script(script_file, {"AMDGCN_ENABLE_DUMP": "1"})
+    asm = _amdgcn_from_stdout(clean.stdout)
+    if _kernarg_preload_length(asm) == 0:
+        pytest.skip("this target does not preload kernel arguments into user SGPRs")
+
+    dump_dir = tmp_path / "dump"
+    dump_dir.mkdir()
+    _run_kernel_script(script_file, {"TRITON_DUMP_MIR": str(dump_dir)})
+
+    mir_files = list(dump_dir.glob("simple_kernel_*.txt"))
+    assert len(mir_files) == 1, "Exactly one MIR file should have been dumped"
+    mir = mir_files[0].read_text()
+
+    assert "firstKernArgPreloadReg" in mir, "MIR should record the first preloaded kernarg SGPR"
+    assert "inreg" in mir, "MIR should keep inreg on the kernel arguments"
+
+
+def test_kernarg_preload_survives_mir_round_trip(tmp_path):
+    """A dump/swap round trip must emit the same code, preload included, and still compute correctly."""
+    script_file = tmp_path / "test_kernel.py"
+    script_file.write_text(_COMPLEX_KERNEL_SCRIPT)
+
+    clean = _run_kernel_script(script_file, {"AMDGCN_ENABLE_DUMP": "1"})
+    clean_asm = _amdgcn_from_stdout(clean.stdout)
+    if _kernarg_preload_length(clean_asm) == 0:
+        pytest.skip("this target does not preload kernel arguments into user SGPRs")
+
+    dump_dir = tmp_path / "dump"
+    dump_dir.mkdir()
+    _run_kernel_script(script_file, {"TRITON_DUMP_MIR": str(dump_dir)})
+
+    # The swap path disables LLVM's machine scheduler by default; re-enable it so the
+    # two runs differ only in whether the MIR took a trip through YAML.
+    swapped = _run_kernel_script(script_file, {
+        "TRITON_SWAP_MIR": str(dump_dir),
+        "TRITON_SWAP_MIR_ENABLE_MISCHED": "1",
+        "AMDGCN_ENABLE_DUMP": "1",
+    })
+    swapped_asm = _amdgcn_from_stdout(swapped.stdout)
+
+    assert _descriptor_directives(swapped_asm) == _descriptor_directives(clean_asm), \
+        "Round-tripped MIR should request the same kernel descriptor, including kernarg preload"
+    assert _normalized_instructions(swapped_asm) == _normalized_instructions(clean_asm), \
+        "Round-tripped MIR should produce the same instruction sequence"

[NVIDIA] Verify MMAv5 barrier predicates and TMEM transfer warp counts (#12666)

Gluon accepts separate lists of MMAv5 completion barriers and
predicates. Require one predicate per barrier for both plain and scaled
MMA so verification catches mismatched lists before the custom printer
asserts.

Require at least four warps for TMEM loads, stores, and initialized
allocations with an explicit register layout. The layout compatibility
check reads two warp basis entries, and a two-warp layout has only one.

Add verifier regressions for a missing completion predicate and a
two-warp TMEM load in `test/TritonNvidiaGPU/invalid.mlir`.

[GPU] Directly dispatch a single unconditional warp specialization (#12664)

Implement `warp_specialize` via the obvious `if/else` when the lowered
kernel has one `ttg.warp_specialize` outside any CFG cycle and its block
dominates every return.
The generic case uses the existing dispatcher.

Partition sizes determine the warp-ID ranges. On NVIDIA, the **effective
register cap** determines which partitions share an entry and restore
path.

For example, assume four default warps and three capture-free worker
partitions. A uses warps 4–7 at 80 registers. B uses warps 8–9 and C
uses warps 10–11, both at 48 registers.

**Before**, the default group publishes one command byte per worker.
Each switch case emits its own register adjustment.

```text
dispatch:
    setmaxnreg.dec(24)
    cta_barrier()
    switch ld.shared.u8(state[warp_id - 4]):
        case A:    run_case(A, 80)
        case B:    run_case(B, 48)
        case C:    run_case(C, 48)
        case EXIT: return

run_case(body, cap):          # expanded separately in each case
    setmaxnreg.inc(cap)
    cta_barrier()
    body()
    cta_barrier()
    setmaxnreg.dec(24)
    goto dispatch
```

**After** Worker partitions avoid the `ld.shared` command and the exit
`cta_barrier()`

```text
setmaxnreg.dec(24)
cta_barrier()
if warp_id < 8:
    setmaxnreg.inc(80)
    A()
    cta_barrier()
    setmaxnreg.dec(24)
else:
    setmaxnreg.inc(48)        # shared by B and C
    if warp_id < 10: B()
    else:            C()
    cta_barrier()
    setmaxnreg.dec(24)
return
```

This saves 2-3% in some kernels.

[GPU] Fold workerless warp specialization before creating TTGIR (#12663)

Call the default Gluon function directly when the worker list is empty.
Require at least one worker partition in ttg.warp_specialize.
